```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(openxlsx)
library(dplyr)

# Read the data
data <- read.xlsx("/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/R:Python scripts/Barchart/Normal+grouped barchart/Normalized FU.xlsx")

# Order factor levels for consistent bar placement
data$Sample <- factor(data$Sample, levels = c(
  "GVR-EHA105-Light", "GVR-C58C1-Light", "GVR-GV3101-Light",
  "T-DNA-EHA105-Light", "T-DNA-C58C1-Light", "T-DNA-GV3101-Light",
  "GVR-EHA105-Dark", "GVR-C58C1-Dark", "GVR-GV3101-Dark",
  "T-DNA-EHA105-Dark", "T-DNA-C58C1-Dark", "T-DNA-GV3101-Dark"
))

# Create group variable for consistent coloring
data$Group <- case_when(
  grepl("GVR-.*-Dark", data$Sample) ~ "GVR-Dark",
  grepl("T-DNA-.*-Dark", data$Sample) ~ "T-DNA-Dark",
  grepl("GVR-.*-Light", data$Sample) ~ "GVR-Light",
  grepl("T-DNA-.*-Light", data$Sample) ~ "T-DNA-Light"
)

# Compute mean and standard deviation
summary_data <- data %>%
  group_by(Sample, Group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rate = mean(`Normalized.FU`),
    sd_rate = sd(`Normalized.FU`)
  )

# Plot
ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = Sample, y = mean_rate)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "grey") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_rate - sd_rate, ymax = mean_rate + sd_rate),
                width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = data, aes(x = Sample, y = `Normalized.FU`),
             color = "black", size = 2) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = rep(c("EHA105", "C58C1", "GV3101"), 4)) +  
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Normalized RLU") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black"),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
library(openxlsx)
library(dplyr)

# ==========================================
# Read Excel file
# ==========================================

df <- read.xlsx(
  "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/Source_data_AgroGem.xlsx",
  sheet = 1
)

# ==========================================
# Keep relevant columns
# ==========================================

df <- df %>%
  select(Sample, `Normalized.RLU`) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Sample),
    !is.na(`Normalized.RLU`)
  )

# ==========================================
# Log10 transform
# ==========================================

df$log10_RLU <- log10(df$`Normalized.RLU`)

# ==========================================
# One-way ANOVA
# ==========================================

anova_model <- aov(
  log10_RLU ~ Sample,
  data = df
)

anova_table <- as.data.frame(summary(anova_model)[[1]])

write.csv(
  anova_table,
  "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/ANOVA_results.csv"
)

# ==========================================
# Tukey HSD
# ==========================================

tukey_result <- TukeyHSD(anova_model)

tukey_table <- as.data.frame(tukey_result$Sample)

tukey_table$Comparison <- rownames(tukey_table)

tukey_table <- tukey_table %>%
  select(
    Comparison,
    diff,
    lwr,
    upr,
    `p adj`
  ) %>%
  arrange(`p adj`)

write.csv(
  tukey_table,
  "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Tukey_HSD_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# ==========================================
# Significant comparisons only
# ==========================================

significant_comparisons <- tukey_table %>%
  filter(`p adj` < 0.05)

write.csv(
  significant_comparisons,
  "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Significant_Comparisons.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# =========================
# 1. Define all file paths
# =========================

genotype_file_paths <- list(
  # Col-0
  AgroGem_WT_1 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/Backbone_comparison/CRISPResso_on_pSG058_Col-0_Dark_whole_plant_Rep1/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  AgroGem_WT_2 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/Backbone_comparison/CRISPResso_on_pSG058_Col-0_Dark_whole_plant_Rep2/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  AgroGem_WT_3 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/Backbone_comparison/CRISPResso_on_pSG058_Col-0_Dark_whole_plant_Rep3/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  Floral_Dipping_WT_1 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/ku70:lig4 floral dipping/Col-0_MC4/Control13/CHLI2_Sample1_rep1/CRISPResso_on_22C_0xHS_MC4_CHLI2_Sample1/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  Floral_Dipping_WT_2 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/ku70:lig4 floral dipping/Col-0_MC4/Non_HS_Control_rep2/CHLI2_rep2/CRISPResso_on_22C_0xHS_MC4_CHLI2_Sample2/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  Floral_Dipping_WT_3 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/ku70:lig4 floral dipping/Col-0_MC4/Non_HS_Control_rep3/CHLI2_Sample3_rep3/CRISPResso_on_22C_0xHS_MC4_CHLI2_Sample3/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",

  # lig4
  AgroGem_lig4_1 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/DNA_repair_mutant_lines/ID318_CHLI2_MC4.1_MC4.8/ID318_CHLI2/CRISPResso_on_pSG022_ID318_CHLI2_Rep1/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  AgroGem_lig4_2 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/DNA_repair_mutant_lines/ID318_CHLI2_MC4.1_MC4.8/ID318_CHLI2/CRISPResso_on_pSG022_ID318_CHLI2_Rep2/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  AgroGem_lig4_3 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/DNA_repair_mutant_lines/ID318_CHLI2_MC4.1_MC4.8/ID318_CHLI2/CRISPResso_on_pSG022_ID318_CHLI2_Rep3/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  Floral_Dipping_lig4_1 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/ku70:lig4 floral dipping/lig4_CHLI2/CRISPResso_on_Floral_dipping_lig4_Rep1/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  Floral_Dipping_lig4_2 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/ku70:lig4 floral dipping/lig4_CHLI2/CRISPResso_on_Floral_dipping_lig4_Rep2/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt",
  Floral_Dipping_lig4_3 = "/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/NGS Results/ku70:lig4 floral dipping/lig4_CHLI2/CRISPResso_on_Floral_dipping_lig4_Rep3/Alleles_frequency_table_around_sgRNA_CGACATTCATAACAGAGACA.txt")


# =========================
# 2. Function to process one file
# =========================

process_genotype_data <- function(file_path) {
  data <- read.table(file_path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", row.names = NULL, fill = TRUE)

  colnames(data) <- c(
    "Aligned_Sequence", "Reference_Sequence", "Unedited",
    "n_deleted", "n_inserted", "n_mutated", "#Reads", "%Reads"
  )

  edited_sequences <- data %>%
    filter(Unedited == "False")

  total_edited_reads <- sum(edited_sequences$`#Reads`, na.rm = TRUE)

  edited_sequences <- edited_sequences %>%
    mutate(Reads_Percentage = (`#Reads` / total_edited_reads) * 100) %>%
    group_by(Aligned_Sequence) %>%
    summarise(
      Reads_Percentage = sum(Reads_Percentage, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  return(edited_sequences)
}

# =========================
# 3. Process all files
# =========================

genotype_data <- lapply(genotype_file_paths, process_genotype_data)

# =========================
# 4. Combine all samples
# =========================

edited_freq_long <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(genotype_data), function(sample_name) {
    genotype_data[[sample_name]] %>%
      select(Aligned_Sequence, Reads_Percentage) %>%
      mutate(
        Sample = sample_name,
        Genotype = case_when(
          grepl("WT", sample_name) ~ "Col-0",
          grepl("lig4", sample_name) ~ "lig4"
        ),
        Method = case_when(
          grepl("AgroGem", sample_name) ~ "AgroGem",
          grepl("Floral_Dipping", sample_name) ~ "Floral_Dipping"
        )
      )
  })
)

# =========================
# 5. Find shared Top 20 sequences, ordered by WT frequency
# =========================

Top_30_Sequences <- edited_freq_long %>%
  group_by(Aligned_Sequence) %>%
  summarise(
    Sum_Edited_Frequency = sum(Reads_Percentage, na.rm = TRUE),
    WT_Edited_Frequency = sum(Reads_Percentage[Genotype == "Col-0"], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Sum_Edited_Frequency)) %>%
  slice(1:20) %>%
  arrange(desc(WT_Edited_Frequency))

sequence_order <- Top_30_Sequences$Aligned_Sequence

# =========================
# Move specific sequences to the bottom
# =========================

bottom_sequences <- c(
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGAG-------------ATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACAT---------------GGTAACGAGATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACATTCAT-----------GGTAACGAGATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAAC--------------GAGATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGA---------------TCTGTT",
  "TA--------------------------ACGAGATCTGTT",
  "-----------------------TGGTAACGAGATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGA--------------------------GATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGAGTACATGGTAACGAGATCTGT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGAGGACATGGTAACGAGATCTGT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGAGAACATGGTAACGAGATCTGT"
)

# Remove them from current order first
sequence_order <- sequence_order[!sequence_order %in% bottom_sequences]

# Add them to the end
sequence_order <- c(sequence_order, bottom_sequences)

# =========================
# 6. Calculate mean and SD across replicates
# =========================

NHEJ_avg <- edited_freq_long %>%
  filter(Aligned_Sequence %in% sequence_order) %>%
  group_by(Aligned_Sequence, Genotype, Method) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Reads_Percentage = mean(Reads_Percentage, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Reads_Percentage = sd(Reads_Percentage, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    SE_Reads_Percentage = SD_Reads_Percentage / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Fill missing sequence × genotype × method combinations with 0
NHEJ_avg <- NHEJ_avg %>%
  complete(
    Aligned_Sequence,
    Genotype,
    Method,
    fill = list(
      Mean_Reads_Percentage = 0,
      SD_Reads_Percentage = 0,
      SE_Reads_Percentage = 0,
      n = 0
    )
  )

# Replace NA SD/SE from single-replicate cases with 0
NHEJ_avg <- NHEJ_avg %>%
  mutate(
    SD_Reads_Percentage = ifelse(is.na(SD_Reads_Percentage), 0, SD_Reads_Percentage),
    SE_Reads_Percentage = ifelse(is.na(SE_Reads_Percentage), 0, SE_Reads_Percentage)
  )

# =========================
# 7. Restore order
# =========================

NHEJ_avg$Aligned_Sequence <- factor(
  NHEJ_avg$Aligned_Sequence,
  levels = rev(sequence_order)
)

NHEJ_avg$Genotype <- factor(
  NHEJ_avg$Genotype,
  levels = c("Col-0", "lig4")
)

NHEJ_avg$Method <- factor(
  NHEJ_avg$Method,
  levels = c("AgroGem", "Floral_Dipping")
)

NHEJ_avg <- NHEJ_avg %>%
  arrange(Genotype, Method, Aligned_Sequence)

# =========================
# 8. Plot with error bars
# =========================

method_colors <- c(
  "AgroGem" = "steelblue",
  "Floral_Dipping" = "darkorange"
)

ggplot(NHEJ_avg, aes(x = Mean_Reads_Percentage, y = Aligned_Sequence, group = Method)) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(
      xmin = pmax(Mean_Reads_Percentage - SD_Reads_Percentage, 0),
      xmax = Mean_Reads_Percentage + SD_Reads_Percentage,
      color = Method
    ),
    height = 0.18,
    size = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Method), size = 1) +
  geom_path(aes(color = Method), size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Genotype, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    position = "top",
    breaks = seq(0, max(NHEJ_avg$Mean_Reads_Percentage + NHEJ_avg$SD_Reads_Percentage, na.rm = TRUE), by = 5)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = method_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Mean Reads Percentage (%)",
    y = "Top 30 Aligned Sequences",
    color = "Method"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# =========================
# 9. Pearson correlation between methods
# =========================

NHEJ_wide <- NHEJ_avg %>%
  select(Aligned_Sequence, Genotype, Method, Mean_Reads_Percentage) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Method,
    values_from = Mean_Reads_Percentage
  )

cor_results <- NHEJ_wide %>%
  group_by(Genotype) %>%
  summarise(
    Pearson_r = cor(AgroGem, Floral_Dipping, method = "pearson"),
    p_value = cor.test(AgroGem, Floral_Dipping)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(cor_results)
```

Figure 2C
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(openxlsx)
library(dplyr)

# Read Cas9 data
data_cas9 <- read.xlsx("/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/R:Python scripts/Barchart/Normal+grouped barchart/Cas9_MC4_rates.xlsx") %>%
  mutate(Nuclease = "Cas9")

# Read Cas12a data
data_cas12a <- read.xlsx('/Users/shengsongguo/Desktop/Zhang Lab/R:Python scripts/Barchart/Normal+grouped barchart/Cas12a_MC4 sites_mutagenesis .xlsx') %>%
  mutate(Nuclease = "Cas12a")

# Combine both datasets
data_combined <- bind_rows(data_cas9, data_cas12a)

# Set MC4 site order
data_combined$MC4_Sites <- factor(data_combined$MC4_Sites,
                                  levels = c("8", "7", "4", "9", "3", "1", "5", "2"))

# Calculate summary statistics
summary_combined <- data_combined %>%
  group_by(Nuclease, MC4_Sites) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rate = mean(`Overall_Mutagenesis_Rate`),
    sd_rate = sd(`Overall_Mutagenesis_Rate`),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot with grouped bars
ggplot(summary_combined, aes(x = MC4_Sites, y = mean_rate, fill = Nuclease)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_rate - sd_rate, ymax = mean_rate + sd_rate),
                position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = data_combined,
             aes(x = MC4_Sites, y = `Overall_Mutagenesis_Rate`, group = Nuclease),
             color = "black", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Cas9" = "#E64B35", "Cas12a" = "#1f77b4")) +
  labs(
    x = "MC4 Sites",
    y = "Overall Mutagenesis Rate (%)",
    fill = "Nuclease"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black", size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black", size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black")
  )


## Similarity calculation: Pearson correlation
# Step 1: Compute average mutagenesis rates by MC4 site and nuclease
avg_rates <- data_combined %>%
  group_by(Nuclease, MC4_Sites) %>%
  summarise(mean_rate = mean(Overall_Mutagenesis_Rate), .groups = "drop")

# Step 2: Pivot wider to have Cas9 and Cas12a side-by-side
wide_rates <- avg_rates %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Nuclease, values_from = mean_rate)

# Step 3: Calculate Pearson correlation
correlation <- cor(wide_rates$Cas9, wide_rates$Cas12a, method = "pearson")

# Print the result
correlation
```


```{r}
# Step 1: Compute average mutagenesis rates by MC4 site and nuclease
avg_rates <- data_combined %>%
  group_by(Nuclease, MC4_Sites) %>%
  summarise(mean_rate = mean(Overall_Mutagenesis_Rate), .groups = "drop")

# Step 2: Pivot wider to have Cas9 and Cas12a side-by-side
wide_rates <- avg_rates %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Nuclease, values_from = mean_rate)

# Step 3: Pearson correlation test
cor_test <- cor.test(
  wide_rates$Cas9,
  wide_rates$Cas12a,
  method = "pearson"
)

# Correlation coefficient
correlation <- cor_test$estimate

# P-value
p_value <- cor_test$p.value

# Print results
cat("Pearson correlation (r):", round(correlation, 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", signif(p_value, 3), "\n")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(pheatmap)

# ============================================================
# 1) Process one file: remove Unedited TRUE, compute edited-only frequency, filter < cutoff
# ============================================================
process_one_file <- function(file_path, sample_name, freq_cutoff = 0.2) {

  df <- read_tsv(file_path, col_types = cols())

  # Remove unedited rows
  edited_df <- df %>% filter(Unedited == FALSE)

  total_edited_reads <- sum(edited_df$`#Reads`, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Edge case: no edited reads
  if (is.na(total_edited_reads) || total_edited_reads == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      Sample = sample_name,
      Aligned_Sequence = character(0),
      Edited_Reads = integer(0),
      Edited_Frequency = numeric(0)
    ))
  }

  edited_df %>%
    group_by(Aligned_Sequence) %>%
    summarise(
      Edited_Reads = sum(`#Reads`, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Edited_Frequency = Edited_Reads / total_edited_reads * 100,
      Sample = sample_name
    ) %>%
    filter(Edited_Frequency >= freq_cutoff) %>%
    select(Sample, Aligned_Sequence, Edited_Reads, Edited_Frequency) %>%
    arrange(desc(Edited_Frequency))
}

# ============================================================
# 2) Run on all files (replicates stay separate as Sample columns)
# ============================================================
edited_freq_long <- imap_dfr(
  genotype_file_paths,
  ~process_one_file(.x, .y, freq_cutoff = 0.2)
)

# ============================================================
# 3) Top 30 sequences by SUM of Edited_Frequency across ALL samples
# ============================================================
top30_sequences <- edited_freq_long %>%
  group_by(Aligned_Sequence) %>%
  summarise(
    Sum_Edited_Frequency = sum(Edited_Frequency, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Sum_Edited_Frequency)) %>%
  slice(1:30)

# Keep only top 30 sequences
edited_freq_top30_long <- edited_freq_long %>%
  semi_join(top30_sequences, by = "Aligned_Sequence")

# ============================================================
# 4) Force specific sequences to the bottom in your exact order
#    (Only affects row order if they exist in the top30 set)
# ============================================================
bottom_sequences <- c(
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGAG-------------ATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACAT---------------GGTAACGAGATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAAC--------------GAGATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACATTCAT-----------GGTAACGAGATCTGTT",
  "TA--------------------------ACGAGATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACATT----------ACATGGTAACGAGATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACAT-----------ACATGGTAACGAGATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGA--------------------------GATCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGA---------------TCTGTT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGAGTACATGGTAACGAGATCTGT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGAGGACATGGTAACGAGATCTGT",
  "TAGCGACATTCATAACAGAGAACATGGTAACGAGATCTGT"
)

# Only keep bottom sequences that are actually present in the top30 list
bottom_present <- bottom_sequences[bottom_sequences %in% top30_sequences$Aligned_Sequence]

# Current top30 order (by summed frequency)
top_order <- top30_sequences$Aligned_Sequence

# All other sequences (keep their original order)
top_keep <- setdiff(top_order, bottom_present)

# Final enforced order
final_row_order <- c(top_keep, bottom_present)

# Apply factor levels to lock row order
edited_freq_top30_long$Aligned_Sequence <- factor(
  edited_freq_top30_long$Aligned_Sequence,
  levels = final_row_order
)

# ============================================================
# 5) Build matrix for pheatmap: rows = sequences, cols = samples (replicates separate)
# ============================================================
mat_for_clust <- edited_freq_top30_long %>%
  select(Aligned_Sequence, Sample, Edited_Frequency) %>%
  arrange(Aligned_Sequence) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Sample,
    values_from = Edited_Frequency,
    values_fill = 0
  )

mat <- as.matrix(mat_for_clust[, -1])
rownames(mat) <- mat_for_clust$Aligned_Sequence

# Keep columns in the same order as genotype_file_paths (if all exist)
mat <- mat[, intersect(names(genotype_file_paths), colnames(mat)), drop = FALSE]

# ============================================================
# 6) Heatmap
# ============================================================
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("white", "#b2182b"))(200)

pheatmap(
  mat,
  cluster_rows   = FALSE,     # keep row order as we defined
  cluster_cols   = TRUE,      # cluster samples (replicates separate)
  color          = my_palette,
  breaks         = seq(0, 20, length.out = 201),  # your template
  angle_col      = "90",
  fontsize_row   = 6,
  fontsize_col   = 8,
  border_color   = NA,
  treeheight_row = 0,
  treeheight_col = 40,
  show_rownames  = TRUE,
  cellwidth      = 12
)
```
